title: Lease-based drain tokens and credit-escrow rollout for capacity-safe Dedicated GPU upgrades
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Rolling upgrades of Dedicated GPU pools currently cause spikes in tenant rejection and latency when node drains collide with autoscaler actions or simultaneous tenant re-placements. We need an orchestration primitive that guarantees (1) deterministic capacity accounting during upgrades, (2) bounded disruption for high-QoS tenants, and (3) a safe rollout path that composes with autoscalers and tenant priority semantics.

Proposal summary: Implement a lease-based drain token system + tenant-credit escrow ledger. Each upgrade wave will acquire transient 'drain leases' for targeted devices; leases reserve eviction budget from a per-pool escrow and emit explicit handshake events to the cluster autoscaler. Autoscaler will consume drain-lease SLOs to temporarily stall scale-to-zero or aggressive downscales for the wave. Tenants receive soft-eviction signals with credits that let them gracefully checkpoint or fail-over to fallback pools. The controller exposes fine-grained rollout gates (per-tenant QoS buckets, region, and model family) configurable from the Console.

Why different: Existing controllers use time-windowed drains and ad-hoc autoscaler pauses. This design centralizes capacity accounting (escrow ledger) and creates an explicit lease handshake that separates 'upgrade intent' from 'eviction execution'. It reduces simultaneous eviction bursts and lets autoscalers make safe decisions based on reserved upgrade credits.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can allocate and release drain leases against a per-pool escrow with audit logs
Autoscaler respects drain-lease signals: it delays aggressive downscaling when outstanding lease budget > 0
Eviction coordinator performs soft-evictions that surface tenant checkpoint hooks and honor tenant credits
Rollout gate config in Console can target: tenant QoS buckets, region, model-family, and individual tenant IDs
End-to-end test: simulated wave upgrade of 200 nodes shows <3% request rejection spike and <10% 99p latency regression for P0 tenants
Can abort wave and release leases cleanly with automatic backfill within 60s
design_decisions: Use lease TTLs (default 10m) to avoid orphaned reservations; controller periodically renews while actively draining
Keep escrow accounting at pool-level to minimize cross-pool coupling; per-tenant credits tracked logically in metadata rather than physical reservations
Autoscaler integration via a small API: /v1/pools/{pool}/upgrade-escrow-status returning reserved_slots and lease_count
Soft-eviction path is opt-in per tenant; tenants without checkpoint hooks fall back to immediate hard-eviction path but consume more credits
Expose a Console-managed rollout-gate object to avoid CLI-only flows and make audits visible to SREs
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype lease token API on test cluster; emit events to a test autoscaler shim (ENG-412468-pr0)
Phase 2 (controller, 2 weeks): implement escrow ledger + lease lifecycle with idempotent operations and audit logs; basic Console config UI (feature-flagged)
Phase 3 (autoscaler integration, 1 week): add small read-only endpoint and update autoscaler shim to honor reserved_slots; end-to-end integration tests
Phase 4 (tenant flows, 1 week): implement soft-eviction handshake and tenant credit accounting; provide SDK hooks for graceful checkpointing
Phase 5 (staged rollouts, 1 week): run canary on non-production pools, run load tests against production shadow traffic, iterate
Phase 6 (GA): enable feature flag for low-risk customers, gradually expand per rollout policy
testing_and_validation: Unit tests: lease create/renew/release and escrow reconciliation
Integration: autoscaler shim + controller in a local cluster; validate behavior under scale-up/down flapping
Chaos test: random node failures during waves to verify lease TTL safety net
Load test: replay production token distribution to ensure ledger scales (target 1k ops/sec per pool)
SLO experiments: synthetic tenants that assert <3% rejection and targeted latency budgets
observability: New metrics: pool_escrow_reserved_slots, pool_lease_active_count, tenant_credit_balance (redacted IDs)
Console dashboard: per-pool escrow graph, active leases timeline, expected backfill ETA
Audit log sink: lease lifecycle events (create/renew/release/expire) routed to logging + BigQuery for post-mortem
Alerting: escalation when lease_utilization > 80% during an upgrade wave or when orphaned leases > 5 for 10m
rollback_and_aborts: Controller exposes 'abort_wave' API that marks leases as aborted and notifies autoscaler to release hold
Abort triggers background backfill that requests immediate autoscaler prioritization for free slots
If abort fails, TTL expiry ensures leases are released within configured window
Create runbook: steps to manually release leases and emergency backfill (link to Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated-upgrades)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Escrow over-reservation may reduce available capacity causing customer impact — Mitigation: conservative default escrow cap (5% of pool) and gradual ramping
Risk: Autoscaler integration complexity across cloud providers — Mitigation: shim layer with provider adapters and fallback to existing pause mechanism
Risk: Orphaned leases creating slow capacity leak — Mitigation: short TTLs + periodic reconciliation job and alerting
Risk: Tenant SDK adoption slow — Mitigation: offer server-side default soft-eviction behavior and a short compatibility window
